2026-12-23.title: Wednesday after the Sunday before Yaldo
readings: All the treasures of wisdom in Christ
He gave power to become children of God
2026-12-23.alt: Season of Yaldo and Denho. The last days of the Twenty-Five Days' Fast.
2026-12-23.verse: But to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God,
theo: The prologue now speaks of rejection and welcome. “He was in the world, and the world came into being through him; yet the world did not know him. He came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him.” There was no room at the inn. But to all who did receive him, “who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God”, born not of blood or of human will, but of God. Christmas is God's offer of adoption.

Paul struggles in prayer for the Colossians and for many he has never met, so that their hearts may be encouraged and united in love, and that they may have “the knowledge of God's mystery, that is, Christ himself, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” The child in the manger looks poor, but in him are all the treasures of God.
outline: Is there room for Jesus in our house?
Point 1 · His own did not accept him
Point 2 · Power to become children of God
The poor child is God's wealth.
“He gave power to become children of God.”
live: Make room in your Christmas plans for someone who would otherwise be alone.
Renew your baptismal promises in prayer tonight.
2026-12-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came to your own and they did not receive you. We welcome you now: make room in our hearts and homes, make us children of God, and show us all the treasures hidden in you. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we receive him, and he gives us the power to become children of God.

quick: The world did not know him; his own did not accept him.

2026-12-23.action: Make room in your Christmas for someone who is alone.
2026-12-23.question: Have I truly received him?

family.explain: Some people did not welcome Jesus. But those who welcome him become God's children.
family.intention: We pray that our family may welcome Jesus at Yaldo.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make room for Jesus in our home this Yaldo?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, in you are hidden all the treasures of wisdom. As we gather two days before Yaldo, help us to receive you and become children of God. Amen.
share: In Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom (Colossians 2:3). How well do I know Christ?
His own did not accept him (John 1:11). Where is there no room for him in my life?
How will I receive him at Yaldo?
pm.resp: Lord, we receive you with joy.
interc: For the Church, that she may receive Christ with faith and love.
For those who do not know Christ, that they may receive him.
For families preparing for Yaldo, that they may make room for Jesus.
For the homeless, who share the lot of the Holy Family.
For our group, that we may become true children of God.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son came to his own. Open our hearts to receive him, and make us your children through faith in his name. Amen.

illus: A young couple in Adoor, expecting their first child, decided to give their Yaldo shopping budget to a family whose house had been damaged by rain. The wife said: “We wanted Jesus to find room in our home this year.”

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Colossians how much he struggles for them and for those at Laodicea, so that their hearts may be encouraged and united in love, so that they may have all the riches of assured understanding and have the knowledge of God's mystery, that is, Christ himself, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge (Colossians 2:1–3).
All the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Christ. Two days before Yaldo, they are hidden in a child about to be born. God hides his greatest treasures in humble places.

Paul warns: I am saying this so that no one may deceive you with plausible arguments (Colossians 2:4). Faith needs both love and understanding. A believer who knows Christ well is not easily deceived.

In the Gospel John writes: he was in the world, and the world came into being through him; yet the world did not know him. He came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him. But to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God (John 1:10–12).

These are among the saddest and most hopeful words in the Bible. The Creator came to his own creation, and it did not recognise him. But to all who received him, he gave the power to become children of God.

In two days we will celebrate his coming. Will we receive him? Let us make room: a good confession, reconciliation, quiet prayer, charity to someone in need. And let us become what he came to make us: children of God. Amen.
kids: Children, there was no room for Jesus at the inn. Make room for Jesus in your heart by saying a prayer every night!
